title: Admission control & priority heuristics - personal notes
content:
Top-level intent:

This is a messy personal sketch for an admission-control + client prefetch prioritization system. Goal: let the ingress layer make fast, explainable decisions about whether to accept, queue, prefetch, or reject work that touches expensive state (KV cache, large model KV, reserved GPU slots). The heuristics should be simple to implement in the edge proxy and tunable via lightweight config.

Problems we want to solve (observed pain):
- Short bursts from many clients kill latency SLOs because batching/backpressure subsystems saturate.
- Some clients prewarm aggressively and waste quantized cache slots.
- Prefetch policies are opaque and sometimes degrade quality by warming wrong keys.
- Reserved capacity customers need stronger admission guarantees (hard SLO), while free-tier should be best-effort.

Design constraints / desiderata:
- Decision must be O(1) per request (no heavy lookups).
- Config-driven: express priority tiers, weighted scoring, and allowed queue size per tier.
- Local fast fallback: if control plane unreachable, edge uses last-known simple policy.
- Observability: every decision emits a small decision tuple (reason, score, policy-id).
- Fairness across tenants: incorporate token cost + recent usage into score.
- Easy to simulate offline.

Sketch: admission_score = weighted sum of signals
signals: {client_priority, recent_success_rate, estimated_token_cost, kv_hotness_flag, queued_length, reserved_slot_flag, region_penalty}
weights: configurable per route / model / tenant-class

Simple policy DSL (human readable-ish):
- Example config snippet (pseudo-JSON):
{
  "policy_id": "tiered-admit-v1",
  "buckets": [
    {"name": "reserved", "min_score": 0.7, "max_queue": 200, "weight_overrides": {"client_priority": 0.6, "reserved_slot_flag": 0.3}},
    {"name": "standard", "min_score": 0.35, "max_queue": 100, "weight_overrides": {}},
    {"name": "best_effort", "min_score": 0.0, "max_queue": 20, "reject_on_overflow": true}
  ],
  "global_weights": {"client_priority": 0.4, "recent_success_rate": 0.25, "estimated_token_cost": -0.2, "kv_hotness_flag": 0.2, "queued_length": -0.1, "reserved_slot_flag": 0.1, "region_penalty": -0.05}
}

Interpretation: compute admission_score = sum(global_weights[signal] * signal_value) then apply bucket matching by min_score and current queue length. If bucket says reject_on_overflow and queue >= max_queue -> immediate reject 429 with reason code. Else enqueue.

Edge simplified scoring (fast integer-ish):
- Represent scores as ints 0..100. Avoid floats at edge.
- client_priority: map tier -> {enterprise: 90, paid: 60, freemium: 30, anon: 10}
- recent_success_rate: moving window success% mapped to 0..100.
- estimated_token_cost: normalize tokens to 0..100 and flip sign.
- kv_hotness_flag: 0 or 75 (prefer hot keys if high).
- queued_length: clamp 0..100 and invert.

Sample admission path (pseudocode):

function handle_ingress(req):
  ctx = extract_ctx(req)   # client id, tenant class, route, expected_tokens, kv_key_hint
  signals = calc_signals(ctx)
  score = 0
  for s,w in global_weights: score += w * signals[s]
  score_int = clamp(round(score), 0, 100)
  bucket = pick_bucket(score_int, route_policy)
  if bucket.reject_on_overflow and queue_len(bucket) >= bucket.max_queue:
    emit_metric("admit.reject", ctx, {"reason":"queue_overflow","policy":bucket.name,"score":score_int})
    return 429, {"error":"overloaded","policy":bucket.name}
  if bucket.name == "reserved" and ctx.reserved_slot_flag:
    assign_reserved_slot(ctx)
    return forward(req)
  if should_prefetch(ctx, bucket, score_int):
    kick_prefetch(ctx)
  enqueue_or_forward(req, bucket)
  emit_metric("admit.accept", ctx, {"policy":bucket.name,"score":score_int})

When to prefetch? rough rules:
- Only if kv_hotness_flag or predicted next-token-entropy high AND estimated_token_cost > threshold AND admission_score >= bucket_prefetch_cutoff.
- Limit prefetch rate per client class.

API shapes for tuning/control plane (fast ops):
- GET /v1/admission/policy/{policy_id} -> returns JSON config (same shape as above)
- POST /v1/admission/preview -> takes list of simulated requests and returns accept/reject/queue decisions for testing
  payload: {"policy_id":"...","samples": [{"tenant":"t-123","expected_tokens":120,"kv_hint":"user:789"}]}
- POST /v1/admission/override -> ephemeral operator overrides: {"client_id":"c-42","action":"force_accept","expires_at":"2026-03-01T00:00:00Z"}

Observability schema (compact):
- decision tuple: {ts, route, client_id_hash, policy_id, bucket, score_int, reason, queue_len}
- sample log event per decision. Keep limited sampling rate for freemium to avoid cost blow-up.

ASCII flow diagram (rough):

[ingress proxy] -> extract ctx -> score -> pick bucket -----+-> enqueue -> dequeue -> runner
                                                      |
                                                      +-> reject/429
                                                      |
                                                      +-> prefetch kick -> kv/coldload -> cache

Edge failure modes / open questions (TODO):
- race between queue_len snapshot and concurrent enqueues - need CAS or approximate quotas? maybe use token-bucket counters per bucket updated atomically in redis or edge local with periodic reconciliation.
- How to version weight changes without negative behavior spikes? suggestion: rollout weights via canary like other configs, but also enforce max delta per rollout window.
- Migration path for existing batching/backpressure stack: don't replace until headers emitted: add a header X-Admit-Decision that downstream can use.
- What is fair accounting for multi-call flows (chat sessions have multiple calls). Option: amortize per-session budget and decrement on each request. Need session-id.

Experiment ideas:
- A/B: baseline (first-come queue) vs weight-based admit. Measure p95 latency, tail queued requests, revenue-weighted accepted fraction.
- Simulate synthetic bursty traffic to assert queue overflow freq by client class.
- Measure prefetch waste: prefetch started vs keys actually used. Add global budget to cap prefetch cost per tenant per minute.

Notes to self / next steps:
- Build a lightweight simulator (Python) that consumes policy JSON and workload traces to predict tail latency and prefetch cost. I should reuse trace generator from redwood-sim repo. Link TODO: grep for trace export.
- Talk to SRE about atomic counters & Redis slots for fast per-bucket queue counts.
- Draft a minimal API for operator overrides and a small UI tile in Console to view admit decisions.
- Consider exposing per-tenant admit metrics in Console with top reasons for reject.

Quick todo list:
- [ ] Prototype score calc in Go in edge-proxy shim (10% perf overhead target)
- [ ] Simulator + smoke tests
- [ ] Draft rollout plan (canary rules, threshold deltas)
- [ ] Instrument decision tuple in tracing span (low-sample for freemium)

Random thoughts / heuristics that might be useful later:
- Use monotonic decaying credit for clients: credit += refill_rate * dt, cost deducted per request (estimated_token_cost). If credit negative -> lower client_priority signal. Helps smooth bursts.
- For chat-style flows, prefer session-affinity: if session established, bump client_priority slightly for next N requests to keep UX smooth.
- Track prefetch hit ratio per kv_key fingerprint to downgrade kv_hotness_flag when hit ratio drops below threshold.
- Keep admission config small enough to fit in edge process env var (avoid heavy RPC on each decision).

End. This is intentionally rough. Will flesh into PR for serving-runtime once simulator gives numbers.

Signed-off: Maya (notes)
